On May 31, the University Commission submitted to the Ministry of Public Education a declaration on the opening of Baku University, a draft law on the establishment of the university in the city of Baku with explanatory notes attached, the university charter, and the staffing plan and budget for the Faculty of History and Philology with an Oriental section and the Faculty of Medicine for the 1919/20 academic year. On the basis of the draft law it submitted to the Ministry of Education, the Commission requested 3.5 million manats for the organization, establishment, and equipment of the university. The government received the documents positively, and despite the very difficult economic conditions in the newly established republic, increased the amount required for the university to 5 million manats and raised teachers' salaries by one-third over the planned level. The Commission's tasks also included adapting the two buildings allocated for the university - the Commercial School and the First Gymnasium - to the educational process before the beginning of the academic year, equipping lecture halls and laboratories, and purchasing furniture, various apparatus and devices, books, and the like.
en.idx.0152: On July 7, the government broadly discussed the package of documents and draft law submitted by the University Commission through the Ministry of Public Education and adopted them with certain additions and amendments.
en.idx.0153: The documents adopted by the government were widely discussed in July and August 1919 in the legislative and budget-finance commissions of parliament and in the factions of the parties represented in parliament. During these discussions, it became clear that within society, the government, and parliament there were also opponents of opening the university. Some of those opposed believed that teaching in Russian would allow the invited Russian professors to conduct a policy of Russification among students. In their view, those scholars would engage less in teaching science and more in missionary activity, carrying out the Christianization and Russification policy of Tsarism. Seeing the situation, V.I. Razumovsky, the chairman of the University Commission, held meetings with influential members of the government and parliament, as well as leading intellectuals who had a voice in society, assuring them that the university's only purpose would be to teach science to the youth.
en.idx.0154: Despite the major obstacles on the path to creating the first European-type university in the Muslim East, the national government and the intelligentsia overcame all difficulties and successfully completed this undertaking. Three months of intense struggle ended on September 1, 1919, at the 70th session of Parliament with the adoption of the law on opening the University. It is especially important to note the service rendered in the adoption of this law by Azerbaijan's enlightened intellectuals and patriotic people. This law, entitled 'On the Establishment of the State University in the City of Baku,' envisaged the opening of four faculties at the University - History and Philology (with an Oriental section), Natural Sciences, Law, and Medicine. Under Article X of the law, the State University in the city of Baku was considered open from September 1, 1919. Taking into account public concern, paragraph 2 of Article II of the law stated that the Turkish (Azerbaijani - editor's note) language would be taught as a compulsory subject in all faculties. Articles VIII and IX of the law were of particular importance from the standpoint of democratic values and equality of rights. They stated: 'Students and auditors of Transcaucasian and other universities... are granted the right to be admitted to the corresponding courses of the Baku University... New students, whether male or female, are admitted on general grounds.'
en.idx.0155: A few days after the adoption of the Law on the Establishment of the University, the rector and deans were elected at a meeting of the University Commission. By the government's decision of September 8, 1919, 'On the Approval of the Rector and Deans of Baku State University,' Vasili Razumovsky was confirmed as rector, Ivan Shirokogorov as dean of the Faculty of Medicine, and Nikolay Dubrovsky as dean of the Faculty of History and Philology.
en.idx.0156: The last meeting of the University Commission was held on September 15, 1919. At the meeting, the Provisional Council and the University Board were established. Thus, the principal staff of the University and its departments were completed. After September 20, in order to recruit missing personnel, Vasili Razumovsky and Nikolay Dubrovsky met a number of prominent scholars in Rostov-on-Don, Yekaterinoslav, and Kharkiv and obtained their consent to come to Baku. Another member of the University Commission, Boris Finkelstein, was sent to Europe to purchase supplies, equipment, literature, and so forth.
en.idx.0157: On September 29, 1919, the University Charter, consisting of 5 chapters and 72 articles, was adopted. The Charter defined the University's organizational structure, the functioning of its scientific and teaching spheres, and the duties and rights of the professor-teaching staff.
en.idx.0158: The Law and the Charter approved by the Parliament of the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic played an important role in the formation of university governance. In both of these documents related to the University, it is important to note an issue that remains significant both for our present day and for our historical past. In both documents, the University's status was defined as a scientific and educational institution vested with autonomy. This fact in itself reflected how deeply the government of the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic, both in essence and in character, was grounded in democratic and humanistic values and treated them with respect.
en.idx.0159: It should be noted that although the University was granted the right to autonomy, this academic freedom did not last very long. While it was preserved in one form or another during the first years of Soviet rule (1920-1922), it was abolished in later years.
en.idx.0160: On November 10, 1919, the first meeting of the University Council was held. At this session, the composition of the professor-teaching staff was approved, and November 15 was declared the first day of classes at the University. The University began operating with the Faculties of History and Philology and Medicine.
en.idx.0161: In the 1919/20 academic year, the University had a total of 1,094 students including free listeners: 877 were regular students and 217 were free listeners. A total of 604 people were admitted to the Faculty of History and Philology (509 regular students), while 490 were admitted to the Faculty of Medicine (368 regular students). The students' distribution by nationality was as follows: 297 Azerbaijanis, 366 Jews, 209 Russians, and 222 representatives of other nationalities (Armenians, Georgians, Poles, Germans, and others).
en.idx.0162: The first classes at the University began at the Faculty of History and Philology on November 15 with Nikolay Dubrovsky's lecture on general history. Vasili Razumovsky recalled that the large lecture hall was completely full; in addition to students, many intellectuals, members of parliament, government representatives, and others were present. This was followed by Professor Lev Zimin's introductory lecture, which aroused great interest among everyone and demonstrated to the public what a great treasure the opening of the University had brought.
en.idx.0163: At the Faculty of Medicine, classes began on November 20, 1919, and the first lecture was delivered by Arkady Oshman.
en.idx.0164: Baku State University began operating with less than half of the academic staff foreseen in the штат schedule - only 44 academics in total, including 12 professors, 3 associate professors, and 1 private docent. The number of Azerbaijani teachers in the University's academic staff was 9. Among them were Academician Mustafa Topchubashov, who later became a world-renowned surgeon, and docent Mahammad agha Shahtakhtinski, the famous publicist who published the Azerbaijani-language newspaper Sharqi-Rus in Tiflis in 1903-1905. Among the political and state figures of the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic, Mahammad Amin Rasulzade and Rashid bey Kaplanov lectured on the history of Ottoman literature, while Deputy Minister Hamid bey Shahtakhtinski lectured on Russian language and literature.
en.idx.0165: The opening of Baku State University was an unparalleled victory of Azerbaijani democratic culture and its representatives, who had struggled against fanaticism, ignorance, and backwardness in certain strata of society. On the occasion of the University's opening, V. Razumovsky wrote: 'Azerbaijan has created its own hearth of enlightenment, and a new bright page has been written in the history of the Turkic people. A new torch has been lit at the crossroads of Asia and Europe.' An article entitled 'The Opening of the Darulfunun' published in the newspaper Azerbaijan on November 17, 1919, stated: '...To say a new nation, a new science, a new philosophy means that every university must also be a new temple... The Azerbaijan university is, of course, a Turkish university, because it has been opened by the Turkish nation, the Turkish Parliament, and the Turkish Government for Turkish youth. The date November 15, when the university begins life and activity, will become the beginning of a new era of progress...'
en.idx.0166: The world-renowned outstanding statesman and political leader, National Leader of the Azerbaijani people Heydar Aliyev, gave a highly objective assessment of the creation of BSU as such an important historical event, saying that the establishment of our university, which has served as a light for Azerbaijani science from the beginning of the century to the present day, is one of the most remarkable events in our people's history. After intense disputes and discussions, the leaders of the Republic achieved perhaps the greatest dream of their lives - they succeeded in creating the independent higher educational institution of an independent state, Baku State University.
en.idx.0167: The Azerbaijan Democratic Republic, which with its first steps proved that it was based on universal human values and established the ideas of democracy and humanism in Azerbaijan's education system, fell victim in April 1920 to Soviet occupation and ideology. From that date onward, although Baku State University, a legacy of the Republic, preserved its existence, it had to pass through long years of turmoil and hardship.
en.idx.0168: Baku State University in the First Decade of Soviet Rule
en.idx.0169: After Soviet rule was established, the Bolsheviks, having abolished the institutions, state symbols, and other attributes created by the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic, also began changing the content of education at the University, which had only just taken its first steps. In the first years of Soviet rule, in accordance with the Bolsheviks' plan for socialist construction, it was envisaged that a 'cultural revolution' would be carried out in the country. The main task of that 'cultural revolution' was to form a new Marxist-Leninist ideology in society. Educational and scientific institutions were assigned exceptional importance in accomplishing this task.
en.idx.0170: The hopes and aspirations connected with Baku State University, created by Azerbaijan's progressive intellectuals on the basis of a national spiritual ethos, were destroyed by the Soviet regime, and the University, falling into the vortex of an entirely different political system, was forced from the day of its founding to move away from the national values it had followed and the democratic path it had embarked upon. In addition, on December 6, 1922, the University's name was changed to Azerbaijan State University. On January 23, 1924, it was given the name of Lenin, the leader of the Bolsheviks. Nevertheless, despite all difficulties, the University honorably fulfilled the mission it had assumed from the very first day even during the years of Soviet rule. Historical processes confirmed that Baku State University, created at the beginning of the twentieth century by the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic and the progressive intellectuals of the era, even under the influence of Bolshevik ideology continued to support national and social progress and became one of the sources of our people's spiritual and cultural values. Over the 71 years of Soviet rule, it remained the most authoritative higher educational institution to which the Azerbaijani people turned for education.
en.idx.0171: Shortly after the occupation - on May 11, 1920 - an order signed by the first Soviet People's Commissar of Education, Dadash Bunyadzade, stated that the educational process at the University, which was becoming one of the main spiritual and ideological centers of society, would be reorganized, links with Soviet Russia would be established, and teachers would be invited from there. In the 1920s and 1930s, scholars were invited to the University from Russia, mainly from the academic staffs and graduates of higher schools in Moscow, Petersburg, Kyiv, Kazan, and Odessa, including scientists with high achievements in scholarship and pedagogy. The first scholars to come to the University in the Soviet period were from Kazan University. Gradually, a strong potential in various fields of science was formed here.
en.idx.0172: Beginning in 1921, increased attention was paid at the University to the training of academic personnel, and dissertation councils that still function today were established.
en.idx.0173: The University's ideological and political direction, scientific activity, and educational work began to be built not in accordance with the interests of the Azerbaijani people, but in line with the interests of the 'workers' and peasants' government' created by the Bolsheviks, on the basis of class orientation and party loyalty. In these processes, on the one hand, some of the University's intellectuals who objected to Soviet ideology were forced into emigration, while another part continued to work in the initial period because of the Bolsheviks' acute need for locally educated personnel. On the other hand, pressure on the University increased and ideological 'purges' were carried out. The majority of the intelligentsia became victims of the mass repressions of the 1930s. The main purpose of all these measures was to shape the rising generation and the republic's qualified personnel in the spirit of Soviet ideology.
en.idx.0174: During the first decade, the main line was the restriction of the University's academic freedom. In these years, the University's Charter was changed four times (1920, 1922, 1923, 1926). Protesting the pressure on the University after the occupation and the changes to the Charter, V. Razumovsky resigned from the post of rector on May 26, 1920. In November of that same year, Professor Sergey Davidenkov, a graduate of Moscow University, was elected rector. However, because of the pressure, he too refused to continue as rector when his elected term ended in September 1923. In that same year, Aleksandr Gulyayev, a graduate of the Faculty of History and Philology of Kazan University and then a professor at the Faculty of History and Philology, was elected rector of the University.
en.idx.0175: In 1923, the need for a process of reconstruction came to the fore on the grounds that some faculties of Azerbaijan State University and the Azerbaijan Technical Institute were not functioning in accordance with requirements, their curricula did not correspond to reforms, and a number of subjects did not meet the demands of the time. The University's new rector, Aleksandr Gulyayev, approached the matter differently, putting forward as the main priority the training of highly qualified specialists and research workers. The reforms that began continued in 1924 with the creation of the Faculty of Pedagogy on the basis of the Faculty of Social Sciences and the Faculty of Natural Sciences and Mathematics, along with related processes. In addition, the University administration was required to renew the Charter and submit it to the Central Committee of the Azerbaijan Communist (Bolshevik) Party for approval. Taking the statutes of RSFSR universities as a model, a unified regulation for all higher educational institutions was prepared. The 'Regulation on Higher Educational Institutions,' approved by a decision of the Council of People's Commissars of the Azerbaijan SSR, was confirmed as the University's charter by the decision of the University Academic Council dated September 28, 1926. The University's right to autonomy was abolished. According to this Charter, the leadership of the University was concentrated in the hands of a governing board of 3 to 5 persons, and higher-education management bodies new for Azerbaijan - subject commissions, section bureaus, and dean's offices - were created. The Charter also restricted the powers of faculties and councils while expanding the authority of the rector and the dean. In the 1923 charter, the University had been envisaged as a scientific and educational center training highly qualified specialists and researchers. By contrast, the 1926 regulation aimed to orient the University's activity toward teaching. This regulation became the fifth charter governing the University's activity until 1930.
en.idx.0176: In 1926, the University's first Azerbaijani rector, Taghi Shahbazi, was appointed. With Taghi Shahbazi's arrival, substantial work was carried out at the University to expand education in the Turkish (Azerbaijani) language, open Azerbaijani sections in the faculties, and recruit Azerbaijani teachers. In order to increase the number of representatives of the local population among students and teachers, the Presidium of the Central Committee of the Azerbaijan Communist Party (Bolsheviks) adopted a special decision. At the same time, it was envisaged that the Pedagogical and Oriental Faculties would be 'Azerbaijanized.' In January 1929, the 'Student Teachers' Institute was organized at the University, enabling senior students to teach junior courses. These measures led to improvements in the quality of education in the native language and an increase in the number of scientific-pedagogical personnel; promising graduates were retained at the University and involved in scientific-pedagogical work; and research works and textbooks in various fields of science were prepared in the native language.
en.idx.0177: According to information from April 1929, 123 of the University's 232 professors and teachers were Azerbaijanis. Looking at the national composition by faculty, it becomes clear that 79% of the staff of the Oriental Faculty, 56% of the staff of the Faculty of Medicine, 45% of the staff of the History-Social Sciences division of the Faculty of Pedagogy, 37% of the staff of the Natural Sciences and Mathematics division, and 30% of the staff of the Faculty of Law were Azerbaijanis. This data reflected the national potential of the period across the taught subjects and scientific fields. In subsequent years, that staff created a basis for the training of national personnel and the development of many fields of science in the Turkish (Azerbaijani) language.
en.idx.0178: Between 1919 and 1929, approximately 1,500 graduates completed their studies at the University. Of these, 1,200 graduated in medicine and the rest in other specialties. Jafar Jabbarli, Adham Shahmaliyev, Hadi Aliyev, Hanafi Zeynalli, Ashraf Huseynov, Vali Khuluflu, Mammadhasan Dadashov, Feyzulla Gasimzade, Hadi Mirzazade, Sara Ashurbeyli, Alisohbat Sumbatzade, Mammad Arif Dadashzade, Ishaq Jafarzade, Jumshud Zulfuqarli, Mirali Akhundov, Jafar Khandan, and other prominent figures of science and culture were among the graduates of that period. They made important contributions to the development of the republic's scientific and educational institutions and various sectors of production.
en.idx.0179: In 1929, the 10th anniversary of the University's founding was celebrated throughout the republic. The jubilee commission was chaired by Gazanfar Musabayov, Chairman of the Council of People's Commissars of the Azerbaijan SSR. Events were held in Baku, other cities of the republic, and the uyezds. The solemn jubilee ceremony was held on January 12, 1930, in the building of today's Opera and Ballet Theatre with the participation of representatives of party and Soviet organizations, the public, and official guests. On the occasion of the University's 10th anniversary, 6 teachers were awarded the academic title of professor and 3 professors were granted the honorary title of Honored Scientist.
en.idx.0180: On the occasion of the jubilee, a series of articles about the University were published in the press, analyzing the educational and scientific environment there and how the University's tasks were being carried out in accordance with the demands of Soviet ideology. Although plans had been envisaged during the jubilee period for the University's reconstruction, the reorganization of its faculties, and its expansion, from April onward discussion began on converting the University's faculties into separate institutes.
en.idx.0181: There were more important considerations behind these reforms and the plans concerning the University. Despite all pressures, the rapid gathering at the University of nationally minded intellectuals with a very high social standing and intellectual level, the potential of a teaching and student body that preserved national consciousness and identity, the emergence of intellectuals thinking about the future of Azerbaijan, the role of some Azerbaijani teachers and students as principal bearers of national ideology, and the transformation of the University into one of the main centers of science and enlightenment all seriously alarmed the Bolshevik leaders, who feared any force with a different outlook. The positive reaction of intellectuals to such landmark events as the First Turkological Congress (Baku, 1926) and the transition to the Latin alphabet (1929) was also considered dangerous for the political regime.
en.idx.0182: The closure of universities in the USSR was also part of the 'cultural revolution' carried out by the political leadership. Measures related to shortening the period of study and sharply increasing the number of workers and peasants among students - especially the fact that entrance examinations for them took on a merely formal character - had a negative impact on the quality of education at the University. The academic staff, who favored traditional university education, openly expressed dissatisfaction with the creation of pedagogical faculties and viewed the departure of faculties from the traditional organization based on specific sciences as a decline in the University's academic level.
en.idx.0183: On July 23, 1930, the Central Executive Committee and the Council of People's Commissars of the USSR adopted a decision on the reorganization of the higher education system. According to that decision, it was planned to create, on the basis of multidisciplinary higher educational institutions, independent sectoral educational institutions capable of providing the country in a short time with the necessary number of specialists. First, by the decision of the Council of People's Commissars of the Azerbaijan SSR dated May 9, 1930, the Faculty of Medicine was transformed into the Medical Institute; then, by the decision of November 19, 1930, 'On the Reorganization, Regionalization, and Transfer of Higher and Higher Technical Schools of the Azerbaijan SSR to the Relevant Economic Bodies and People's Commissariats,' the University's activity was terminated, and new independent institutes were created on the basis of its separate faculties - the Azerbaijan Medical Institute, Azerbaijan Pedagogical Institute, Institute of Soviet Construction and Law, and Azerbaijan Trade Cooperation Institute.
en.idx.0185: A year after the University's closure, the Soviet and party leadership of the Azerbaijan SSR concluded that such a step had not been correct. The republic needed highly qualified specialists with university education and research staff. The leadership's coming to this conclusion was greatly influenced by the April 1931 decision of the Central Committee of the All-Union Communist Party (Bolsheviks) 'On the Main Tasks of Universities.' That decision acknowledged that the previously dominant opinion that there was no need for university education in the higher-school system had been mistaken and recognized the idea that universities should play the leading role in this field. In a letter from the leadership of the Higher Pedagogical Institute to the Culture and Propaganda Department of the Central Committee and to the collegium of the People's Commissariat of Education of the Azerbaijan SSR entitled 'Proposals from the Higher Pedagogical Institute on the Organization of Azerbaijan State University,' it was emphasized that opening the university was necessary not only for better study of the process of socialist construction but also for the training of highly qualified scientific and pedagogical personnel.
en.idx.0186: Finally, on May 25, 1934, the Council of People's Commissars of the Azerbaijan SSR adopted the decision 'On the Opening of Azerbaijan State University.' Under this decision, on September 1, 1934, the university consisting of the Faculties of Physics and Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry, and History began operating in order to train highly qualified specialists in general scientific disciplines as well as teachers. Mammadkazim Alakbarov was appointed rector of the newly reopened University. After the University was restored, the number of teachers working there, including Azerbaijani teachers, increased year by year; in 1935, 52 teachers worked at the University, 22 of them Azerbaijanis. By the 1938/39 academic year, the number of teachers had increased by approximately 3.5 times to 180, while the number of Azerbaijanis had grown by somewhat more than four times compared with previous years, reaching 91. The number of teachers defending candidate or doctoral dissertations rose significantly. Specialists with high academic titles were invited to the University both from various research institutions of the republic and from outside it. As a result, the composition of the academic staff underwent a fundamental qualitative change. If in 1935, out of 52 teachers, 10 were professors, 14 associate professors, 10 teachers, and 13 assistants, then in the 1938/39 academic year, among 180 teachers there were 21 professors, 31 associate professors, 37 serving in associate professor positions, 63 teachers, and 28 assistants. Although the number of Azerbaijani students increased year by year, this process remained quite slow. As in all higher educational institutions of the USSR, teaching activity at the University was regulated by the normative documents of the Communist Party and the Soviet government concerning higher education.
en.idx.0187: The repressions of the 1930s did not bypass Baku State University. During those years, the Azerbaijani people were effectively deprived of an entire generation of brilliant figures constituting the intellectual wealth of the nation. This was also a policy of destroying the nation's gene pool formed over decades and severing moral ties between generations. From this advanced scientific and educational institution of the republic, more than 100 professors, researchers, and teachers, along with up to 20 students, were unjustifiably subjected to investigation, intimidated, persecuted, exiled, or shot. Those who had headed the University in different years - Taghi Shahbazi (1926-1929), Museyib Shahbazov (1929), Maqsud Mammadov (1929-1930), Mammadkazim Alakbarov (1934-1935), and Balabey Hasanbayov (1935-1937) - were arrested and executed, while Huseyn Guliyev (1937) was arrested and sentenced to five years of exile. Other University administrators also became victims of repression, including the academic secretary, the secretary of the party organization, the chairman of the trade union organization, the head of the Scientific Library, the deans of the Oriental and History faculties, and six department heads.
en.idx.0188: In 1937, one of the most difficult years in the University's history, its rector was Aziz Mammadkarim oghlu Aliyev, an outstanding public and political figure who occupies a special place in Azerbaijan's education system. Despite the blows it received during the repressions, the University, having directed all its potential toward the republic's peaceful construction, not only continued its traditional activity during the years of the Second World War but also had to mobilize all its strength for an entirely new task - assisting in the defense of the country and humanity against a cruel and merciless enemy. The years of the Second World War occupy a special place in the history of the University, whose activity from the day of its foundation had taken shape under various political and ideological factors. Faced with new and complex tasks related to the country's defense, as well as serious difficulties and severe trials, the University's professors, teachers, staff, and student youth displayed dedication from the very first days.
en.idx.0189: On the first day of the war, the University's rector Cebrayil Alasgarov, graduates of the 1940/1941 academic year, and many students and teachers voluntarily joined the army. Overall, during the war years, 1,385 members of the University's student and teaching body were mobilized into the armed forces. Of these, 159 were academic workers, 23 were postgraduate students, and 1,141 were students. Two hundred of the mobilized members of the University collective were women. The mass participation of the University's professor-teaching staff and students in military-defense work also expanded.
en.idx.0190: Because of the complicated wartime conditions, several higher educational institutions of the Azerbaijan SSR were temporarily merged with the University - in October 1941, by the joint decision of the Central Committee of the Azerbaijan Communist Party and the Council of People's Commissars of the Azerbaijan SSR, the Azerbaijan Pedagogical Institute named after V.I. Lenin; later, the Correspondence Pedagogical Institute; at the end of 1941, the Institute of National Economy named after K. Marx; and in December of the same year, the Azerbaijan State Institute of Physical Culture and the Institute of Foreign Language Teachers. As a result of these mergers, which greatly expanded the University, new faculties were organized within it: Economics, Law, Foreign Languages, and Physical Education. Because several higher educational institutions had been merged into the University, its administrative and teaching buildings and dormitories were located approximately 2 km apart from one another. Whereas the University had previously been housed in 7 buildings, during the war it temporarily handed over several buildings to military authorities because of military necessity.
en.idx.0191: Despite the severe conditions of the Second World War, the University's professor-teaching staff spared no effort to preserve and further develop higher education in Azerbaijan. One of the most important events in the University's history during these years was the creation of the Department of Azerbaijani History. Alongside the existing difficulties, the Faculty of Geology and Geography, the Oriental Section within the Faculty of Philology, and departments of the History of the Peoples of the Near East, Near Eastern Languages, and Philosophy were established. Main attention was directed toward solving defense-oriented scientific and technical problems and increasing Soviet patriotism. During the war period, the University largely succeeded in ensuring its own supply of professor-teaching staff and later even rendered special services in the organization of the Azerbaijan Academy of Sciences. The University not only emerged honorably from the harsh trials of the war, but also made an important contribution to victory over the enemy. Among the scientific research works carried out by University scholars during the war years, the work of Yusif Mammadaliyev was of particularly great importance. The new method he invented for producing the main component of aviation fuel had major military significance, and in order to implement it immediately in production, a factory producing that component by the new method was built in Baku. Professor Abdulla Garayev, for his part, proposed a methodology for using Naftalan oil as a wound-healing and pain-relieving remedy. Through the scientific achievements of the University's scholars in strengthening the country's military-defense power and developing the national economy, by training hundreds of highly qualified specialists, and by their active participation and dedication in the defense of the republic, they won the deep esteem of the people. This in turn gave impetus to the University's postwar development.
en.idx.0192: The leadership of Abdulla Garayev, Jafar Khandan Hajiyev, Yusif Mammadaliyev, and Shafayat Mehdiyev - valuable intellectuals and great organizers of education and science - over the University in 1944-1965 created a new stimulus for the development of this institution of higher education. During the years in which they led the University, special attention was paid to training highly qualified specialists and scientific-pedagogical personnel. Results were also achieved in the process of forming scientific schools. At that time, the educational and scientific-creative process of the University, strengthening the material and technical base, and training personnel for foreign countries were priority issues. The University focused primarily on developing personnel training, increasing the number of students, and improving their academic performance.
en.idx.0193: After the Second World War, as throughout the republic, persecution, pressure, and repression also took place at the University. Interestingly, in this educational institution not only teachers and students but even departments were closed as victims of repression.
en.idx.0194: It must be acknowledged that University teachers played an important role in shaping the courage to raise a voice against injustice and the trampling of national dignity within the people, as well as in forming an independent worldview. Among the University's graduates - later leading figures of the republic's science and culture - Khudu Mammadov, Bakhtiyar Vahabzade, who worked at the University for a long time, Ogtay Eldagaz, Ismayil Shikhli, and others, together with a number of officials, organized a secret 'National Liberation Headquarters.' Such well-known figures as Yusif Mammadaliyev and Sadig Rahimov, then Chairman of the Council of Ministers, were also active in this organization. By various means, they tried to direct the activity of state officials toward preserving the people's historical memory and national interests. In those years, alongside other factors, the active work carried out by Azerbaijani intellectuals was of great importance in preventing Armenian plans to annex Nakhchivan and Nagorno-Karabakh to Armenia. In the 1960s, a new generation of fighters for national freedom was emerging in Azerbaijan. In this respect, the University's youth stood out in particular. In the 1950s and 1960s, the University's teachers honorably fulfilled the duties that fell upon them in preserving the people's roots and historical memory and in increasing its scientific and intellectual potential, thereby justifying the hopes placed in them.
en.idx.0195: The arrival of the prominent statesman Heydar Aliyev to the leadership in Azerbaijan had a great impact on preserving this environment that had formed at the University. Within the limits of the ideology of the time, Heydar Aliyev not only prevented the national spirit in Azerbaijan from being completely suppressed, but on the contrary, using all opportunities to the maximum for its development, he gave impetus to the future transformation of the idea of national statehood into a major driving force. Despite persecution and pressure against nationally minded figures of science and culture in the country, through his courage and unwavering will, Heydar Aliyev created favorable conditions in the republic for creative people to think freely and express their views openly, and for ensuring sovereignty and independence in Azerbaijan's history of statehood.
en.idx.0196: This process did not remain without trace in social consciousness; it found reflection in scholarly research and new scientific approaches. For this reason, a major stage of rise in the development of Baku State University began precisely during this period. That period played an important role in the University's development. Heydar Aliyev paid special attention to the university from which he had graduated. For the first time after the University's 10th anniversary, another jubilee was held on his initiative. The state-level celebration of the 50th and 60th anniversaries of Azerbaijan's temple of science and education became important events in the University's history. On the occasion of the 50th anniversary of its founding, in recognition of its services in the development of science and in training highly qualified specialists, the University was awarded the Order of the Red Banner of Labor by the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the USSR on February 11, 1971, and on March 13, 1980, in connection with its 60th anniversary, it was awarded the Honorary Diploma of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the Azerbaijan SSR.
en.idx.0197: In the 1970s and 1980s, broad opportunities emerged at the University for achieving new development and progress, for all-round expansion and improvement of its activity. This became possible first and foremost as a result of the republic's leadership's efforts and policy aimed at achieving the maximum possible independence within the USSR. It was specifically in those years that favorable conditions were created for strengthening the University's material and technical base, improving teaching, developing science, and expanding international relations; an information-computing center was opened; and new academic buildings, laboratories and departments, a library, dormitories, and other facilities were commissioned.
en.idx.0198: Heydar Aliyev emphasized that Azerbaijan's modern development was possible precisely on the basis of the achievements of this educational institution. The National Leader viewed this issue as a priority direction of state policy. For that reason, the University always remained at the center of the care shown to education.
en.idx.0199: At the jubilee event held on November 1, 1969, in today's Shahriyar Club on the occasion of the University's 50th anniversary, the participation of the country's leader Heydar Aliyev and his delivery of a speech in the native language became a turning point in the awakening of the national spirit not only for the University collective, but for all of Azerbaijani society. This speech lit a lamp of hope in the hearts of the University collective, who had suffered from the repressions and persecutions of the totalitarian Soviet regime up to that time, and marked the beginning of a new qualitative stage in the University's life.
en.idx.0200: Heydar Aliyev also paid special attention to enabling talented Azerbaijani youth to study at the leading and prestigious higher educational institutions of the former USSR. In the early 1980s, every year 1,000-1,400 Azerbaijani young people were sent outside the republic to receive higher education. Among them were students of the University as well. Some of the young people who returned after completing their education were provided with jobs at the University.
en.idx.0201: In 1980, the University had 12 faculties preparing personnel in 18 specialties and 64 specializations, a faculty for the education of foreign citizens, a faculty for the advanced training of higher- and secondary-school teachers, a preparatory department, 89 departments, 4 problem laboratories, and an interuniversity scientific-research computing center. At that time, more than 13,000 students were studying at the University. Important work was carried out to improve the quality of education and develop science, and its international relations expanded. For this purpose, new structures were created, and the University's Humanities Building was commissioned.
en.idx.0202: During this period, the University was the main center in the formation of the Azerbaijani people's intellectual potential. Of the 1,137 members of the professor-teaching staff, 116 were doctors of sciences and professors, including 7 corresponding members of the Azerbaijan Academy of Sciences, and 311 were associate professors. Among these scholars, who rendered great services in the development of all spheres of Azerbaijani society, were figures of state, science, and culture. Academicians Mammad Arif Dadashzade, Feyzulla Gasimzade, Ismayil Huseynov, Alisohbat Sumbatzade; professors and doctors of pedagogical sciences Ahmad Seyidov and Agammad Abdullayev; doctor of historical sciences Adham Shahmaliyev; honored scientist Sara Ashurbeyli; and Ishaq Jafarzade, the first researcher of our material culture and the discoverer of the Gobustan rock carvings, among others, made invaluable contributions to Azerbaijani science.
en.idx.0203: At the same time, a number of structural changes were made at the University: departments of Civil Procedure and Financial Law (1985), Methods of Teaching Chemistry (1987), Mathematical Cybernetics (1988), Folklore (1989), Mathematical Methods of Control Theory (1990), Operations Research and Mathematical Modeling, and Probability Theory and Mathematical Statistics (1990) were created, as well as the M.M. Huseynov Museum of Archaeology and Ethnography (1986), and research laboratories entitled 'Forecasting, Prospecting, and Evaluation of Gold Placers' (1989), 'World Azerbaijanis: Historical Demography' (1989), and 'History of the Material Culture of Azerbaijan' (1989).
en.idx.0204: Despite the processes taking place in Azerbaijan, political developments that began in Soviet society as a whole from the mid-1980s further deepened the crisis that existed in the economic, public, social, and spiritual spheres, as well as in national relations. None of the measures undertaken by the ruling Communist Party to prevent the country's collapse produced the expected result; on the contrary, 'perestroika' and 'glasnost' brought all the contradictions of the Soviet empire into even sharper relief. They accelerated its collapse and gave a powerful impetus to the development of the democratic movement.
en.idx.0205: The unstable and complicated situation that existed both in the republic and at the University in those years is also evidenced by the fact that between 1987 and 1991, there were three new appointments to the post of rector at the University. Naturally, this could not but negatively affect the harmonious rhythm of teaching and scientific research at the University. Nevertheless, as always, the University - distinguished by its rich traditions and by the selfless intellectuals working in the fields of science and education - withstood all difficulties and honorably continued the historical mission it had assumed from the moment of its founding. As a result, the University came to stand at the forefront of the Azerbaijani people's national liberation movement.
en.idx.0206: In the late 1980s, when Armenian separatist actions in Nagorno-Karabakh were intensifying and Azerbaijanis were being forcibly expelled from the lands of Western Azerbaijan now called Armenia, the indifference and incompetence of the republic's leadership deeply disturbed University employees, just as they disturbed every patriotic son and daughter of Azerbaijan. Despite all the pressure mechanisms of Soviet ideology, there were many freedom-loving and combative people active at the University. Thanks precisely to their activism, University students were among the principal participants in the mass rallies held in Baku at that time. The main aim of these young people was to prevent the trampling of our people's rights, expose the insidious plans of Armenian provocateurs and their patrons, and preserve the territorial integrity of the republic. In the lecture halls, discussions were held around Azerbaijan's independence, ties with the Turkic world, and other topics. In January 1988, the University's students held the first protest action against the forced deportation of our compatriots from Armenia. The University allocated its teaching-production base in the Quba region to accommodate refugees. A special account called 'Yardım' ('Aid') was opened to meet their needs, and considerable funds were raised by the collective. In front of the University's main academic building, the professor-teaching and student collective held regular crowded rallies, while professors and teachers also appeared regularly on radio, television, and in the press.
en.idx.0207: Because of the situation that had arisen in the republic, despite preparations it was not possible to hold the University's 70th anniversary jubilee. Taking into account numerous demands, on October 27, 1989, the University's Academic Council decided that it should be named Baku State University and that the street on which it was located should be given the name 'University.' By the decision of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet of the Azerbaijan SSR dated February 19, 1990, and the order of the Minister of Public Education dated March 1, 1990, the University's historical name was restored.
en.idx.0208: In the events of January 20, written in golden letters into the history of our country's struggle for freedom, members of the University's teacher and student collective were also among those in the front ranks resisting the invading army units. After the tragedy as well, the University collective actively participated in the mass protest actions held in the republic.
en.idx.0209: Despite all this, devoted commitment to science and education made itself felt. Since the ideas of Marxism-Leninism and the dogmas based on them, which had failed in practice, had plunged society into a crisis, it became necessary to shape public consciousness on the basis of the demands of the new era and completely reorganize the humanities education system.
en.idx.0210: Despite the difficulties, reforms were being carried out to improve the quality of teaching and scientific research and to optimize management. In those years, the University's branches in Lankaran and Sheki were established, and in order to train personnel in accordance with the demands of the time, the Faculties of International Relations and International Law, and Social Sciences and Psychology (1991), as well as a number of new departments and laboratories, were created on the basis of the Faculty of History.
en.idx.0211: Baku State University in the Period of Independence
en.idx.0212: On October 18, 1991, the Supreme Council of the Republic of Azerbaijan adopted the Constitutional Act on the State Independence of the Republic of Azerbaijan. The political processes that occurred in the early years of independence had a negative impact on the life of the republic as a whole, including the University. The academic rhythm of educational processes at the University was disrupted, and a decline was observed in the quality of education and the conduct of scientific research. Cases of students absenting themselves from classes increased. The mass participation of students and teachers in the fighting for Karabakh, the difficult situation on the front, the increase in the number of killed, and the general tense political processes in the country affected the University. The professor-teaching staff and students provided all kinds of assistance to the wounded, families of the killed, and displaced and internally displaced persons. On the other hand, negative developments in education, the creation of numerous private universities without material and technical facilities, and the prevailing disorder and chaos in the country brought the educational process close to a standstill.
en.idx.0213: With the 1992 'Education Law' of the independent Republic of Azerbaijan providing for higher education to transition to a multi-level (bachelor's, master's) system, BSU began transitioning to a dual-level education system starting in the 1993/1994 academic year. In the same year, BSU began teaching at the bachelor's level for the first time, and in 1997, at the master's level. In accordance with the demands of the era, starting in 1992, philosophy, history of philosophy, religious studies, Islamic studies, ethics, aesthetics, political history, sociology, political science, political economy, and economic studies were added to the series of socio-political and economic sciences to be taught. Significant changes were made to the University's structure in connection with the multi-level education system, and new faculties, departments, departments, and scientific research laboratories began operating. From 1992, an English department was established at BSU.
en.idx.0214: The strategic course implemented in education following National Leader Heydar Aliyev's return to leading the country, like other educational institutions, ensured BSU's future development. The increase in funding allocated to the University each year and student admissions provided conditions for conducting important educational reforms, expanding the university's human potential, strengthening the material and technical base, and forming a new structure. Beginning the revival period, BSU recovered its role as the leading higher educational institution of an independent state and as an important scientific and educational center. This situation enabled it to establish relations with world-leading higher educational institutions and scientific centers. The organization of higher education in accordance with international standards at the University fostered the continuation of training specialists for foreign countries during the independence period.
en.idx.0215: In accordance with the Presidential Decree of June 13, 2000, 'On Improving the Education System in the Republic of Azerbaijan,' BSU was granted the status of a higher education institution operating on the principle of self-governance.
en.idx.0216: The most important assessments related to the University's activities were made during its anniversaries. The University's 75th (1994) and 80th (1999) anniversaries were solemnly celebrated by the Presidential Decree and personal participation of Heydar Aliyev, President of the Republic of Azerbaijan. Following each jubilee event, new reforms have been undertaken at the University.
en.idx.0217: The prominent statesman Heydar Aliyev's strategy regarding Azerbaijan's future development, as well as his policy on the development of culture, science, and education, is successfully continued by the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Mr. Ilham Aliyev. He shows special attention and care to the University and its transformation into a modern educational complex. With his care, BSU began reorganizing its activities in accordance with the requirements of the new era and began playing an important role in implementing educational reforms in the country.
en.idx.0218: At present, the organization of education at the University is carried out in accordance with state development strategy. The tasks placed on education by state programs are determined as the main direction, and the policy of ensuring development in all sectors to increase the quality of education and science is pursued.
en.idx.0219: Starting from the 2003/2004 academic year, a multi-point system for assessing students' knowledge was introduced at BSU. Important work has been done in improving the education system at BSU, increasing the quality of higher education, developing student and faculty mobility, and expanding international relations. On May 19, 2005, Azerbaijan joined the Bologna Process and became its full member. In accordance with the 'Model Regulations on the Organization of Teaching Using the Credit System in Higher Educational Institutions' approved by the Ministry of Education of the Republic of Azerbaijan on April 20, 2006, the credit system began to be gradually introduced in all faculties of the University and was fully completed in 2009.
en.idx.0220: In accordance with the provisions of the European Credit Transfer System and the Bologna Declaration, the procedures for ensuring academic mobility of students and postgraduates studying at BSU, the right to study freely at other higher educational institutions within the country and foreign countries, and the determination and recognition of the equivalence of credits earned by students in specialties at their educational institutions are formalized through special commissions at the faculties.
en.idx.0221: One of the most important developments in the University's structure was taking steps to transform it into a research university. In this regard, after a long time had passed since the opening of the first institution (Institute of Applied Mathematics, 1991), the establishment of the Research Institute for Physical Problems under BSU on the basis of scientific research laboratories operating in the Faculty of Physics was an important milestone (2005).
en.idx.0222: A series of changes and reforms have been carried out in the management structure to improve the quality of scientific research and to reorganize education. On the basis of the 'State Program for the Development of the Creative Potential of Specially Gifted Children (Youth) (2006-2010),' under BSU's auspices, the 'Young Talents' Lyceum, the Faculty of Ecology and Soil Science, the Turkology Research Laboratory, the Nanotech Research Laboratory, Barama Media Center, the Quba teaching-practice and recreation center, the BSU Gazakh branch, the modern Teaching Television Studio at the Faculty of Journalism, and many other institutions began operating. As a continuation of structural changes, the Science and Education Center at the Institute of Geography and Agrochemistry of the National Academy of Sciences of the Faculty of Ecology and Soil Science (2015) and the BSU Public Oversight Council (2016) were established; the Gazakh branch of the Azerbaijan State Pedagogical University was placed under BSU's authority (2016).
en.idx.0223: Along with these changes, significant work has been done to raise science and education to world standards and their integration. During the years of independence, BSU, having made significant contributions to the development of Azerbaijan's education and science, has also gained prestige in the international community in terms of the effectiveness of scientific research. Important theoretical and practical research on urgent problems of natural and humanitarian sciences are carried out in the University's faculty, department, and scientific structures (institutes, centers, and laboratories). These research projects are distinguished not only by their relevance but also by their broad scope and priorities. Baku State University actively participates in various international projects and exchange programs (EU TEMPUS-TACIS, ERASMUS MUNDUS projects, Mevlana and Orhun exchange programs covering Turkic states, and others). As a result of increased attention to science and education, there has been a significant increase in the number of scientific papers published by University scholars in journals indexed by international agencies. At the same time, important work is being done to communicate to the world community at prestigious international conferences the results of research carried out in Azerbaijan and at the University. The University's relations with international agencies and publishers (Clarivate Analytics agency, Elsevier academic publishing, and others) have created extensive opportunities for colleagues.
en.idx.0224: In 2016, BSU received the highest award for science development from the Clarivate Analytics agency and the Science Development Foundation under the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, and the 'SCOPUS Award' established for the first time in Azerbaijan by Elsevier academic publishing and the Science Development Foundation under the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan. Along with this, the 'Applied and Computational Mathematics' journal published at BSU, as the only impact-factor journal in the republic, also received the 'SCOPUS Award.' As a continuation, in 2018, BSU and several of its employees received the 'Web of Science Azerbaijan-2018' joint awards from the Clarivate Analytics agency and the Science Development Foundation under the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, and the 'Super Award' as the leading publisher among universities in Web of Science was also awarded to Baku State University. In recent years, the number of scientific papers published by University scholars in journals indexed by international information agencies and citations of these papers have increased at an accelerating pace, which is clear evidence not only of the quantitative growth but also of the relevance and quality indicators of the research conducted and the results obtained.
en.idx.0225: Seeking to occupy an appropriate place in the international higher education system, BSU has been systematically working in recent years on introducing distance communication technologies into educational processes, preparing teaching-methodological materials on distance education, creating an automatic management system based on modern information technologies (an 'Electronic University'), expanding the exchange of experience with world-renowned universities, inviting renowned foreign scholars and scientific and educational figures, expanding the contingent of foreign and doctoral students, and carrying out other appropriate measures.
en.idx.0226: One of the reforms implemented in Azerbaijan's education system was the creation of SABAH groups on the initiative of the Ministry of Education of the Republic of Azerbaijan. The main purpose of this was to prepare educated, skilled, and well-prepared young specialists who would contribute to the development of Azerbaijan, and to implement the training of competitive specialists in the local and international labor markets. SABAH groups at BSU have been operating since the 2014/2015 academic year.
en.idx.0227: Along with the construction process underway at the University and the course of reforms, the commissioning of a new building in 2008 was an important event. The attendance of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Ilham Aliyev, at the opening ceremony reflected his highly valuing the role played by the University in the country's science and education.
en.idx.0228: In 2017, by the appropriate order of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Baku State University was granted the status of a Public Legal Entity.
en.idx.0229: The 90th and 100th anniversaries of the University were also celebrated with great pomp. The President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Ilham Aliyev, participated in both events, and in his meeting with the University collective highly valued the historical mission of the University toward our people.
en.idx.0230: On the occasion of BSU's 100th anniversary, a series of events were held both in our republic and in foreign countries. On this landmark occasion, scientific conferences and round tables were organized at the BSU Gazakh branch, Mingachevir State University, Azerbaijan State University of Economics, Azerbaijan Medical University, Sumgait State University, Azerbaijan State Pedagogical University, Baku Engineering University, Lankaran State University, and a number of other scientific and educational institutions. This was commemorated at UNESCO (12.06.2019, Paris), ISESCO, and international associations of universities (28-29.05.2019, Bucharest. 'InterUniversity Cooperation for Open Science' International Conference), and other international organizations and bodies (10.09.2019, Vienna, Azerbaijan Cultural Center). To immortalize the jubilee date, a silver jubilee coin with a nominal value of 5 manats was issued by the Central Bank, a BSU jubilee stamp was produced, and books were published on the 100th anniversary of BSU.
en.idx.0231: By Presidential Decree, the '100th Anniversary of Baku State University (1919-2019)' jubilee medal of the Republic of Azerbaijan was instituted, and for their services in the development of education and science in Azerbaijan, a number of BSU employees were awarded honorary titles, orders, and medals.
en.idx.0232: As state attention to BSU increases, modern educational reforms are carried out, and new scientific achievements are made, its international reputation has risen, and many world-renowned prominent figures have been deemed worthy of the title of Honorary Doctor of BSU. For demonstrating care for the advancement of science and education at the University, raising its name and prestige to higher levels, and rendering invaluable service before the Azerbaijani people and state, by the decision of the BSU Academic Council dated October 28, 1994, the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Heydar Aliyev, was deemed worthy of the title of Honorary Doctor of Baku State University.
en.idx.0233: At the 90th anniversary event of the University, the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan, Mr. Ilham Aliyev, was presented with the Honorary Doctor diploma of BSU. The presidents of the Republic of Turkey, Turgut Ozal, Suleyman Demirel, Abdullah Gul, and the presidents of Turkmenistan, Saparmurad Niyazov, and Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov, the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan, Islam Karimov, the Prime Minister of the Republic of Turkey, Mesut Yilmaz, the former national security advisor of the U.S. President, a prominent public and political figure, and the world-renowned political scientist Zbigniew Brzezinski, the Chairman of Ukraine's Supreme Rada, Volodymyr Lytvyn, President of Latvia, Vaira Vike-Freiberga, the world-renowned Azerbaijani writer Oljas Suleimenov, President of Romania, Traian Basescu, the rector of Moscow State University named after M.V. Lomonosov, Academician V.A. Sadovnichy, Pakistan's Prime Minister, Muhammad Nawaz Sharif, and other prominent state and scientific figures were deemed worthy of the title of Honorary Doctor of BSU.
en.idx.0234: The 44-day victory campaign of the Glorious Azerbaijan Army, which entered Azerbaijan's history as the Patriotic War and was led by President Ilham Aliyev, the Victorious Supreme Commander-in-Chief, during the Patriotic War came to represent a showcase of the successful execution of Azerbaijan's worthy contribution to the Glorious Victory. During the fighting, the faculty, staff, and students of Baku State University rallied together as one fist around the policy pursued by the President and made their proper contribution to the Glorious Victory. From among the students and graduates of the University who participated in the battles, 22 were martyred.
en.idx.0236: Baku State University (BSU) continues to successfully fulfill its fundamental mission of preparing highly qualified specialists and ensuring that our country occupies a worthy place in the world's scientific and cultural space. Currently, the University is taking substantial steps in five directions - education, research, innovation and commercialization of scientific knowledge, social activities, and expanding international relations. The University is taking various measures to participate in the country's socio-economic development, forming the human potential required in in-demand specialties, and serving technological progress. Modernizing in accordance with contemporary challenges, it carries out specialist training at international standards. As a result of continuing this process, the University's integration into the unified European scientific and educational space is accelerating, its international ranking and reputation are increasing, and its competitiveness and development are ensured.
en.idx.0237: Educational programs at all levels (bachelor's, master's, doctoral) are prepared and updated jointly with specialists from industry and business enterprises. Specialists from production facilities are involved in teaching and scientific activities, master classes and scientific seminars are organized. Through such cooperation, the needs and demands of the labor market are studied. New specialties are determined, and specialists are trained in these specialties taking into account the scientific and pedagogical potential. Under the 'Code for Future' project, through partnership with 'Code Academy' and 'DevEducation' with the support of the Ministry of Science and Education, conditions were created for BSU students to enhance their knowledge in programming, system administration, and network administration in classrooms equipped with modern computers.
en.idx.0238: Today, BSU graduates show the highest results in teacher recruitment (MIQ) examinations, 'Advancement' competitions, and other international and republican-level competitions, and at the same time, our students and lyceum students occupy leading positions in international, regional, and local olympiads and knowledge competitions.
en.idx.0239: The 'Blackboard' learning management electronic system is successfully implemented at the University. Currently, through this system, student knowledge assessment, video recording of classes, and convenient access to information through mobile applications are implemented, and the process of continuous analysis of student and faculty activity is carried out.
en.idx.0240: In recent times, in order to effectively organize scientific activity at the University, the content of ongoing scientific research has been updated, its quality has been improved, and positive results have been achieved in directing the results directly to their application areas. The results obtained by BSU scholars in scientific research institutes, laboratories, and departments have been included in important reports and valued as having practical significance. Taking into account the growing demand in our country for higher education specialists with convergent-innovative knowledge and practical skills, BSU has expanded its existing relations with production enterprises, aligned the scientific research directions of its faculties, scientific research institutes, centers, and laboratories with BSU's 2021-2030 Strategic Development Plan, and prioritized fundamental and applied directions.
en.idx.0241: In 2021, for the first time, the Center of Excellence for Research, Development, and Innovations was established, which, taking as the basis the principles of linking education-science-production and the commercialization of scientific results, expanded relations with industry and production. At the Center of Excellence, the establishment of new industry-oriented scientific research laboratories such as Industrial Chemistry, Bioengineering, Microbiology and Virology, Astrocosmical and Atmospheric Research, and Digital Research, Cell Culture and Genome Editing, Materials Science, and Biological Anthropology has further strengthened the organization's activities. A number of commercial research project contracts in the oil and gas industry have been signed.
en.idx.0242: To more broadly involve students in scientific research, promote their scientific activities, increase their public participation, and support their social projects, the activities of student scientific societies, student organizations, and student clubs have been expanded. The Student Scientific and Technical Creativity Center, established in 2021, lays the foundation for scientific initiatives and scientific research. As a result, teams of students, postgraduates, and young researchers working in the Center regularly achieve high success at the 'TECHNOFEST' Aviation, Space, and Technology Festival.
en.idx.0243: Work is being done to foster creativity in students by solving non-standard tasks through joint cooperation and team work and instilling skills to share their individual knowledge. They are provided training and events are organized in the directions of implementing scientific ideas, patenting them, gaining recognition, and expanding their application, as well as expanding their social initiatives. Specialists working in industry are involved in teaching, and master classes and lectures by specialists working in scientific research institutes and universities of various countries (Turkey, USA, Great Britain, Italy, Kazakhstan, Ukraine, Japan, Romania, Germany, Hungary, Czech Republic, etc.) are organized.
en.idx.0244: The University's international relations expand and develop on the most diverse platforms. In recent times, BSU has signed cooperation agreements and agreements on dual degree programs at bachelor's, master's, and doctoral levels with Bilkent University, Ankara University, Istanbul University, Caucasus University, and other universities in Turkey, Izmir Institute of Technology, Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg in Germany, Berlin Technical University, Anhui University in China, South Bohemia University in Czech Republic, Tashkent State University of Law in Uzbekistan, Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies, Russian University of Economics named after G.V. Plekhanov, Kyungpook National University in South Korea, Al-Farabi Kazakh National University in Kazakhstan, Atyrau State University, University of the Punjab in Pakistan, Holon Institute of Technology in Israel, Hebrew University of Jerusalem (HUJI), Lincoln University in the USA, Tomar Polytechnic University in Portugal, Business and International Studies University in Switzerland, and other universities.
en.idx.0245: In accordance with the 'State Program for Increasing the International Competitiveness of the Higher Education System in the Republic of Azerbaijan for 2019-2023,' BSU implements 12 international dual degree programs at the bachelor's, master's, and doctoral levels using world science's leading scientific and educational achievements to train specialists appropriate to labor market demands, in cooperation with leading universities and institutions in countries such as the USA, Germany, Israel, Sweden, Kazakhstan, and others. BSU strengthens its position in international rankings. BSU currently ranks 565th in the 'QS World University Rankings 2027: Top Global Universities,' compiled by one of the world's most prestigious ranking agencies in the field of higher education, 'Quacquarelli Symonds' (QS). BSU has been awarded 5 stars ('excellent') in the 'QS Stars' audit conducted by 'QS Quacquarelli Symonds.' According to the results of the 'THE Sustainability Impact Ratings 2026' published by another prestigious world ranking organization, the 'Times Higher Education' (THE) agency, BSU is placed in the 101–200 band, ranking among the world's top 200 universities.
en.idx.0246: Along with international relations, special emphasis is placed at BSU on domestic cooperation. To involve the scientific potential possessed by the University in solving the country's social problems and implementing socio-economic programs, relations are expanded with the country's state institutions, prestigious enterprises, and public associations, and joint social projects are implemented. Cooperation plans are drawn up with partner organizations, and high-level conferences, seminars, and other events dedicated to the scientific, cultural, socio-economic, and other problems of the country are held at the University. Throughout last year, a series of events was held at BSU dedicated to the study of the Heydar Aliyev heritage and Azerbaijani ideas, state youth policy, humanitarian issues, and the promotion and preservation of national and spiritual values.
en.idx.0247: To study the current demands of the labor market, the main skills required of specialists in the new era, ensure that these demands are taken into account in specialist training, create university-industry cooperation, involve specialists working in industry in the educational process, allow students to gain new standards of practical experience in production, and carry out joint projects and scientific research, BSU is currently maintaining cooperation with about 70 state, private, and non-governmental organizations and implementing large-scale joint social projects.
en.idx.0248: These relations are established with state bodies and private companies and are directly aimed at the effective organization of educational processes and scientific research activities, as well as providing employment for graduates. Agreements have been signed with the Ministry of Justice, the Prosecutor General's Office, the Supreme Court of the Republic of Azerbaijan, the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources, the State Service for Antimonopoly and Consumer Market Protection, the Ministry of Defense Industry, the Space Agency of the Republic of Azerbaijan (Azercosmos), the Media Development Agency of the Republic of Azerbaijan, the Audiovisual Council of the Republic of Azerbaijan, the National Depository Center of the Azerbaijan Stock Exchange, the Intellectual Property Agency, the Bar Association, the Mediation Council, the State Service for Property Matters, the Agency for the Development of Small and Medium-Sized Businesses (SMEDA), the DOST Agency, the National Observatory for Labor Market and Social Protection Issues, the Social Services Agency, the Quality Assurance Agency in Education, the Student Education Credit Fund, the Education Development Fund, the National Library of Azerbaijan, LU-MUN HOLDING, bp-Azerbaijan, AzerGold, PASHA Bank, 'PASHA Insurance,' 'PASHA Life Insurance,' 'Bayramli Group,' 'TURKSOY,' the International Foundation for Turkish Culture and Heritage, 'Xazar TV' LLC, 'ARB 24' television channel, the Karabakh Revival Fund, and other organizations. It is no coincidence that as a result of the development of BSU's relations, in recent years many national and international grant and contractual projects have been implemented, and numerous students, doctoral students, and young researchers have been represented in these projects.
en.idx.0249: As one of the main partners of social projects, serving as a platform where the ideas and initiatives of state institutions, scientific, cultural, economic, and other institutions and creative associations are presented and discussed, the University creates opportunities for presenting humanitarian and social programs and social initiatives to the public. BSU scholars actively participate in the country's public life, the professor-teaching staff and prominent scholars conduct social research, and are implementing country-level social projects.
en.idx.0250: As part of collaboration with employers, special practical rooms have been established at BSU - 'NewsLab' studio of 'ARB 24' television channel, Azerbaijan Press Council office, 'Turkish Room,' 'Debate Room' of 'Xalq Gazeti,' special auditorium of the Media Development Agency, special auditorium of the Azerbaijan National Library, and with support from 'bp-Azerbaijan' company, 'BSU Publishing House' and the Useful Minerals Museum have been renovated.
en.idx.0251: The reforms carried out, modern dormitory facilities provided in recent years - a 5-story, 220-bed 'Student Space,' 'Book House,' Foreign Language Center, 'Student Space,' 'ECO-SPACE,' 'EcoEnergy' station, provision of modern textbooks and educational materials, and opening of a series of new specialties and specializations in undergraduate and graduate programs considering labor market requirements, implementation of dual diploma programs with prestigious world universities, etc. serve to improve the quality of teaching and scientific research, increase students' public participation, and shape them as genuine citizens dedicated to Azerbaijanism and national-spiritual values.
en.idx.0257: "I am very happy to be a graduate of Baku State University."
en.idx.0259: National Leader of the Azerbaijani People
en.idx.0261: As an alumnus of the Faculty of History of Azerbaijan State University, Heydar Aliyev remained in contact with the University throughout his life and never neglected his concern for this educational institution. This stemmed from his loyalty to the University he graduated from, his love for intellectuals, and his dedication. Regarding any decision related to BSU, from the holding of its jubilees to the recognition and awarding of University staff, Heydar Aliyev approached every matter with special sensitivity, never withholding his attention from this first temple of science and education of the republic. He is the most famous alumnus who elevated both the Azerbaijani people's and the University's reputation to great heights and rendered invaluable service to his nation. The 50th, 60th, 75th, and 80th anniversaries of the University were held with the participation and leadership of National Leader Heydar Aliyev.
en.idx.0262: Heydar Aliyev's election as the leader of the republic in 1969 marked the beginning of a great turning point and a period of national awakening in Azerbaijan's history. The invaluable contribution of the achievements gained by our people to the restoration of state independence in the late 20th century is an indisputable fact. The important historical stage spanning 1969-1982 played a kind of bridge role between the period of the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic and the national liberation movement rising in the late 1980s in the republic. As a result of Heydar Aliyev's wise policy in the republic, the strong social, economic, and intellectual potential created over 14 years became the foundation for the restoration of Azerbaijan's independence.
en.idx.0263: During 1970-1980, just as in other spheres, significant qualitative changes occurred in science, education, culture, and social-cultural sectors. Noting that the republic's progress was possible with a sufficient number of educated, national cadres, Heydar Aliyev paid special attention to the development of higher education in Azerbaijan, expanded its network, increased the number of students, and showed concern for teachers. As a result, the material and technical base of higher education institutions was strengthened, equipment and various supplies were purchased, and dormitories were built. All of this gave impetus to raising the level of education in Azerbaijan.
en.idx.0264: During these years, new development and progress at the University, comprehensive expansion and improvement of its activities became possible due to the efforts of the republican leadership aimed at maximum independence within the USSR and the policy pursued. Precisely during those years, favorable conditions were created for strengthening the University's material and technical base, improving the quality of teaching, developing science, expanding international relations, opening a computer and computation center, constructing new educational buildings, laboratories and departments, library, dormitory, etc.
